items.text: Optimize session dropdown

thread.text: Analyzing this item and researching the codebase...

Research complete. Three concrete optimization targets found: (1) Every dropdown open fires TWO round-trips — a GET /sessions?limit=50 (even though the list is already rendered from cache) plus a POST /sessions/refresh that is a no-op returning changed:false outside hybrid mode. The 15s poll already keeps the cache fresh, so opens are doing redundant work. (2) Keyboard support stops at the trigger: Enter/Space toggles and Escape closes, but rows aren't focusable and there's no arrow navigation — switching sessions is mouse-only. (3) The 50-row cap is hard-coded in the fetch URL AND enforced server-side (limit le=50); pinned sessions always show, so only older unpinned ones get trimmed, and sessions beyond 50 are unreachable from the dropdown (the Sessions page has them). Before proposing a plan, three questions: 1) What motivated this item — slow open, keyboard-only switching, finding sessions past the cap, or all of it? 2) For keyboard work: arrows + Home/End + Enter-to-switch (plus type-ahead) acceptable, with the full search-bar footer left to the separate related item? 3) Keep the 50-row cap, or add a load-more/pagination path so older sessions stay reachable?

qa.research_notes: ui/chat/js/session-list.js renders rows (pin, family carets, status, kebab/trash) and fetches via /api/v1/db/sessions?limit=50 (+ include_hidden). ui/chat/js/session-init.js owns open/close: _loadSessionList() calls populateSessionSelect() (GET) + refreshSessionMetadata() (POST /sessions/refresh) on EVERY open. Keyboard handling exists only on the trigger (Enter/Space toggle, Escape close) — no arrow navigation over rows. The 50-row cap is hard-coded in the fetch URL. Sessions Page (ui/main-panel/sessions) has the full list + recycle bin + restore, so the dropdown is the quick-switch surface. POST /sessions/refresh is a hybrid-mirror sync (app/api/db_viewer.py:473) that returns {"changed":false} immediately when no hybrid backend is configured — a wasted round-trip on every open in the default local setup. The server enforces limit le=50 (app/api/db_viewer.py list_sessions); pinned sessions are fetched without a limit, so only older unpinned sessions are trimmed. refreshSessionMetadata() refetches only when changed; the 15s poll (menu closed, session-init.js:1342) already keeps _sessionsCache fresh, so the GET on open is largely redundant.

items.text: Add search bar and recycle-bin toggle to session dropdown footer (search session names incl. recycled; content search later, low priority)

thread.text: Analyzing this item and researching the codebase...

Research complete. The dropdown footer (.session-manage-row) already hosts manage actions (show-hidden eye, checkbox batch-delete); the session fetch (GET /sessions?limit=50) never returns recycled sessions and caps at 50, so covering recycled sessions needs at least a small backend addition. Three questions posted.

Q1) Search should match session names across ALL sessions — including ones past the 50-row cap and recycled ones — which needs a small backend addition (q + include_recycled params on /sessions). OK to touch the API, or should search only filter what's already loaded?
→ Yes all sessions and content. It needs to mimic the session page search

Q2) When a search query is active, should recycled matches appear automatically (with a 'bin' badge, like the Sessions page cross-catalog search), or only when the recycle-bin toggle is on?
→ Yes there should be a bin flag and click to restore just like session page

Q3) In recycle-bin mode, how should restoring work: a per-row restore button, click-the-row-to-restore, or a two-click confirm like the Sessions page?
→ Just show the bin flags and click to restore similar to how they're presented in search results

Plan ready: backend q + include_recycled params on /sessions (title search across all sessions incl. bin, no truncation when searching); dropdown footer gains a search bar with Title/Content mode chip and a recycle-bin toggle; recycled rows get the Sessions-page bin badge with two-click restore; content mode ports the Sessions page message scan (session-messages endpoint, chunked + cached).

Done — search bar and recycle-bin toggle shipped in the session dropdown footer. Backend: /sessions gained q (title LIKE, escaped) + include_recycled params; search lifts the 50-row cap (all matches, hard cap 200) and bin rows are flagged recycled:true. Frontend: search bar with Title/Content mode chip + clear, recycle-bin toggle beside the eye/checkbox, bin-badge two-click restore, content-mode message scan ported from the Sessions page (chunked + cached). Also fixed a stale search-debounce race that could hide sessions after clearing the query. Verified: node --check both JS files, Python syntax, SQL validated against real DBs.

plan.approach: Mimic the Sessions page search + recycle-bin behavior inside the session dropdown. Backend: add q (title LIKE, no truncation while searching) and include_recycled (bin rows returned, each flagged recycled:true) params to GET /sessions, relaxing the limit cap to 200 so search truly covers sessions past the old 50 cap. Frontend: the dropdown footer (.session-manage-row) gains a search bar with a Title/Content mode chip and a recycle-bin toggle; recycled rows render the Sessions-page 'bin' badge with two-click restore (POST /sessions/{id}/restore); content mode ports the Sessions page message scan (/session-messages?light=1, chunked, cached, match-count chip). Search state lives in module state so the 15s poll and re-renders preserve it.
steps: db_viewer.py list_sessions: add q (title contains, escaped, LIKE) and include_recycled params; include bin rows (flagged recycled:true) when include_recycled OR q is set; skip the 50-row truncation while q is active (all matches returned) and bump the hard cap to 200 so the dropdown can request more when searching/bin mode; select s.status to derive the flag; verify no-q/no-recycled behavior is unchanged
session-list.js: module state _searchQuery/_searchMode/_binMode/_msgIndex/_msgScanBusy; populateSessionSelect appends q + include_recycled + limit=200 when active; map recycled into cache entries

session-list.js: _renderSessionRows filters by query (title/agent match, or content match count in content mode) and by bin mode (only recycled rows when toggled with no query; merged with bin badges while searching); recycled rows render the bin badge (two-click restore) and hide trash/kebab; content matches get a match-count chip

session-list.js: port _scanMessagesForQuery from the Sessions page (fetch /session-messages per session with the same light=1 filters, chunked at 8, in-flight query superseded, _msgIndex cached, progressive re-render) with the same constants (min query 2, scan cap, fetch limit)

session-init.js: handlers for search input (debounced ~200ms → set _searchQuery → populateSessionSelect + content scan), mode chip toggle, bin toggle (set _binMode → refetch), and the bin-badge two-click restore (arm 'Restore?' 3s, second click POST /sessions/{id}/restore, refetch + toast 'Session restored'); Escape inside the search input clears the query first instead of closing the menu
app1.css: style the search input, mode chip, bin toggle and bin badge with design-system variables (both themes); keep the sticky footer layout intact and let the input shrink the row buttons

Verify: node --check on both JS files, JSON/param sanity on the API (q returns only matching incl. bin; include_recycled flags rows; default unchanged), manual browser pass (title search, content mode, bin toggle, two-click restore, search survives the 15s poll, dark+light themes)

Search results beyond the old 50-row cap now surface (by design) — the fetch is heavier while a query is active (limit=200, no truncation)
Keyboard nav: the search input must swallow arrows/Enter/Escape while focused so typing doesn't switch sessions or close the menu
Bin rows get restore only — the trash button is hidden on them to avoid a confusing no-op recycle; bulk delete stays active-only
storageAdapter.isBrowser path (hybrid/browser storage) has no server q — search/bin filter client-side over the adapter rows (recycled flag read from the adapter data if present)

Verified: node --check both JS files; Python syntax check; SQL logic validated against real DBs (default excludes bin == live total_count 15; q returns recycled matches; include_recycled surfaces bin; LIKE escape holds)
Live-server verification (limit=200 / q / include_recycled on the running API) — requires a server restart to load the backend change

BUGFIX: stale search-debounce race made the dropdown hide sessions. Type in the search box, then clear within 200ms (× or Escape) — the pending debounce timer resurrected the old query and silently filtered the list while the input looked empty; the eye toggle's fresh refetch is why sessions 'sometimes' reappeared. Fix: _setSearchQuery cancels any pending commit, input debounce centralised in session-list.js (_scheduleSearchCommit), and closeMenu cancels pending commits. Verified: node --check both files; live API default returns every non-hidden/non-recycled session (all hidden:false); DB has 0 active-but-hidden sessions.

Rows + footer rendered by ui/chat/js/session-list.js (_renderSessionRows/_appendManageRow); footer = .session-manage-row (sticky, app1.css:6484) with eye toggle (show hidden), checkbox-mode toggle, delete-selected. Fetch: populateSessionSelect() -> GET /api/v1/db/sessions?db=local.db&user_id=..&limit=50 (+include_hidden=1 in manage mode); server list_sessions (app/api/db_viewer.py:1589) caps limit le=50, always excludes status='recycled' (line 1698), has NO search param. Recycle = soft delete (status='recycled', cascades children); restore endpoint POST /api/v1/db/sessions/{id}/restore (db_viewer.py:1110). Sessions page (ui/main-panel/sessions) has the full list + recycle-bin view + cross-catalog search + two-click restore chip (sessions-page.js:1156/1191) as precedent. Footer handlers in ui/chat/js/session-init.js:720-739; the 15s poll (session-init.js:1424) calls populateSessionSelect, so search/bin state must live in module state and be re-applied on every refetch. Adding q (title LIKE) + include_recycled params to list_sessions is additive and mirrors the existing search param pattern (db_viewer.py:4044).

items.text: Model selector to have effort too
Clean up chat_ui buttons
Fix rendering dupe and reorder bugs
Fix lazy loads
Stabilize voice recording: only show mic option when browser supports it

thread.text: Analyzing this item and researching the codebase...

Research complete. The mic button (#chat-voice-btn) is rendered unconditionally via the mic_send control in chat_ui.json; support is only checked on click inside startSpeechDictation (native SpeechRecognition, or MediaRecorder + getUserMedia with server LLM transcription, per the /api/v1/auth/ui-config voice policy). On unsupported browsers the button still shows and just pops an error alert — this item reverses that. A ready-made hook exists: the .no-voice pill class (used by the web-chat sign-in gate) already hides the mic and forces send-only. Two questions before the plan:

Q1) Should the mic hide only in the main chat composer, or also in the other places it appears (Gen UI page toolbar, app-config assistant, secondary search pills)?
→ it should hide everywhere where browser mic is not supported

Q2) On non-HTTPS addresses (e.g. LAN over http) the mic APIs are unavailable — hide the button there too, or keep showing it with the existing ‘requires HTTPS’ alert on click?
→ yes hide it there too

Plan ready. Hide the mic everywhere voice input is unsupported (no SpeechRecognition AND no MediaRecorder+getUserMedia, or a non-secure context) via one shared isVoiceInputSupported() in attachments.js applied at every mic-button wiring site — the main composer reuses the existing .no-voice CSS hook to go send-only; Gen UI pill, app-config assistant and secondary pills hide the button directly. Review the plan to start the change.

Done — implemented. isVoiceInputSupported() in ui/shared/js/attachments.js now gates every mic button: the main composer (#chat-input-row), Gen UI page pill and ability-search pill go send-only via the existing .no-voice CSS hook; the app-config assistant and the legacy voice element hide the button directly; forwardChatPillControls never forwards to a hidden mic. Covers non-HTTPS and unsupported browsers (no SpeechRecognition AND no MediaRecorder), plus an async refinement that hides the mic when LLM dictation is disabled and there is no native SpeechRecognition. All five edited files pass node --check.

plan.approach: Centralize the voice-support decision in one exported helper (isVoiceInputSupported in ui/shared/js/attachments.js) that mirrors startSpeechDictation's runtime matrix, and call it at every mic-button wiring site so the button is hidden (not click-to-alert) wherever voice is impossible: insecure context (non-HTTPS), or no SpeechRecognition AND no MediaRecorder+getUserMedia. The main chat composer (#chat-input-row) reuses the existing .no-voice CSS hook (app1.css:3786) to become send-only; the Gen UI page pill, app-config assistant and secondary search/chat pills hide their voice button directly. An async policy refinement (reusing the cached /api/v1/auth/ui-config voice policy) also hides the mic when the admin has disabled LLM dictation AND the browser has no native SpeechRecognition — the exact case startSpeechDictation would otherwise error on.
steps: attachments.js: export isVoiceInputSupported() = window.isSecureContext && !!(SR || (navigator.mediaDevices?.getUserMedia && window.MediaRecorder)); in initAttachments(), when unsupported add 'no-voice' to #chat-input-row (existing CSS hides #chat-voice-btn and forces send visible); when supported, run async refinement via _loadVoicePolicy(): if policy.llm_enabled === false && !SR, hide too
genui-toolbar.js: in the Gen UI page pill builder, when !isVoiceInputSupported() hide the voice button (hidden + inline display:none important, the wake-lock pattern)
page-assistant.js: same guard on the app-config assistant composer's voice control
dom-utils.js: same guard in the secondary search/chat pill builder (voiceBtn wiring at ~line 1447)
voice.js (element module): same guard in init() so a config that lists the legacy 'voice' control never renders an unsupported mic

Verify: grep all #chat-voice-btn / voiceBtn wiring sites to confirm none are left unguarded; confirm the predicate matches startSpeechDictation's paths (native SR, LLM recorder, llm-disabled, insecure-context); JS syntax check; no chat_ui.json change needed (mic_send stays configured — CSS handles the send-only swap)
risks: On non-HTTPS (LAN http) the mic disappears entirely in the main composer — intended per Q2; the old 'requires HTTPS' alert path becomes unreachable from the main pill (still used by startSpeechDictation if called programmatically)

A mic-only pill mode config (chat-pill-mic-only) would override .no-voice (its !important rule comes later in app1.css) — current config always uses mic_send, so unaffected; documented for future config authors
The LLM-disabled refinement is async, so an unsupported mic could flash for a frame at boot in that edge case; the sync capability check covers the common cases instantly
Legacy chat-footer-config.js / chat-header-config.js also reference the mic but are replaced by chat-controls-config.js — left untouched (inert)
Reversible: the button reappears automatically in any browser/context where voice works; no config or data changes
plan.research_notes: Decisions from Q&A: (Q1) hide everywhere the browser mic is unsupported — all four wiring sites in scope; (Q2) also hide on non-HTTPS, dropping the 'requires HTTPS' alert path for the button. Support predicate mirrors startSpeechDictation (attachments.js:499-520): voice works iff (!useLlm && SR) || (useLlm && canRecord), where useLlm depends on the ui-config voice policy; the sync helper approximates the default policy (browser_then_llm) and the async refinement matches the exact runtime decision. .no-voice already proven in production by the web-chat sign-in gate and dash-adder pill.

execution_log.step: attachments.js: isVoiceInputSupported() exported (secure-context + SR/MediaRecorder matrix); initAttachments() adds no-voice to #chat-input-row when unsupported, with async LLM-policy refinement
genui-toolbar.js: Gen UI page pill goes send-only (no-voice) when voice unsupported

Verified: node --check passes on all 5 edited files; every mic wiring site guarded

qa.research_notes: Mic button = #chat-voice-btn (static DOM in ui/chat/chat-side-panel.html:286), mounted via the mic_send control in data/config/chat_ui.json (chat_pill right zone in desktop + mobile active_footer and idle_footer). applyChatPillLayout (ui/shared/js/chat-pill-config.js) shows mic + send together; CSS (.chat-pill.has-text) swaps mic out for send when the input has text. Click is wired in ui/shared/js/attachments.js initAttachments() -> startSpeechDictation(), which holds the canonical support matrix: SR = window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition; canRecord = !!(navigator.mediaDevices?.getUserMedia && window.MediaRecorder); server voice policy fetched from /api/v1/auth/ui-config (voice_dictation_llm_enabled, voice_dictation_mode browser_then_llm | llm_only), cached in _loadVoicePolicy(). Paths: native SR when !useLlm && SR; recorded audio + LLM transcribe when useLlm && canRecord; otherwise error alerts (llm-disabled / insecure-context / unsupported). attachments.js:93-96 documents the CURRENT deliberate behavior: keep the button visible even in an insecure or very old browser so clicking explains the limitation — this item reverses that decision. Ready-made hook: app1.css:3786-3787 already has .chat-pill.no-voice .chat-pill-voice { display:none !important } and .chat-pill.no-voice .chat-pill-send { display:inline-flex } (used by the web-chat sign-in gate and dash-adder pill); nothing ever adds no-voice to the main pill today. Note: the light-mode + mode-class rules (chat-pill-mic-only etc.) could fight .no-voice if the pill ever runs mic-only mode — current config always uses mic_send, so the swap stays send-only. Element module ui/chat/elements/voice.js only serves the legacy 'voice' control name (not in any current config row) and has no support check; wake-lock.js shows the established hide-when-unsupported pattern. items.text: Restore chat pill drag handle (footer handle exists in code but not visible)

thread.text: Analyzing this item and researching the codebase...

Root cause found. The handle (#chat-footer-handle) and its CSS both exist and nothing clips them, but the JS visibility checks keep hiding it. Two checks decide visibility: _updateFooterHandleVisibility() in ui/chat/js/chat-ui.js and the checks in ui/chat-controls/chat-controls-config.js (_buildActiveFooter + switchFooterMode active branch). All three only inspect DIRECT children of #chat-footer-row for the data-header-control attribute. Since the row-layout refactor, footer buttons live nested inside generated .chat-header-row[data-controls-row] > .chat-header-zone > button — so they are never direct children — and manifest-driven controls like wake_lock carry data-element-origin instead of data-header-control. The check always evaluates false, the handle gets display:none, and the drag/click toggle is dead. Fix: query descendants via r.querySelectorAll('[data-header-control], [data-element-origin]') in all three spots. Plan proposed — review it to start the change.

Done. Both files pass node --check. The handle will now be visible whenever the footer row has controls (active mode) and hidden in idle mode — which is the intended behavior.
